chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Who was in the studio and Freddy Jenkins's precise playing
summary: Holmes recognizes his solo on 'Keep Your Business to Yourself' and judges a sloppy trumpet solo to be someone other than Freddy Jenkins.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Can you remember who was in the studio? Or anybody that... Because there have been so many names suggested.
Yeah. Now, who was there? Well, Freddy Jenkins was on one of the numbers. I mean, he was in the studio -- Freddy Jenkins, the trumpet player.
Did he come in with Morton. Because he certainly wouldn't...
Well, I don't know who he come in with. But he was there.
Because he wouldn't have been there with Russell.

No. Well, he could have been with Morton. I guess all the rest of the fellows that were there that wasn't with Russell was with Jelly Roll. But there was a gang of them in there. I can't remember all of them. In fact, there's very few of them I can remember. Right now I can't think of nobody's name.
But you recognized your own playing on one of the records.
I can't always tell my playing, but I know that was my playing. Usually the ones that I mistake for me sometimes, they're much better players than I am. But they sound bad, then I know it's me.
Well, I think it's a great solo, and it's on "Keep Your Business To Yourself." Now, Crawley brought in music.
Yes, he brought his music in. All we had to do was just play it. He passed out the music, and we'd play it. It was written out, yeah. Now, what else?
Some of the trumpet playing you thought might have been Lincoln Mills.
Well, yeah, one number I heard, it sounds similar to Freddy Jenkins, but I would say it's not Freddy

Jenkins -- definitely not. Freddy was too clean in his playing. He was very precise, but he was very clean. This playing was fast, the notation was fast, but it was not clean -- it was sloppy. Freddy was not a sloppy trumpet player. He was very precise, and anything he hit at, he hit it. The notes were clear.
You said when he executed triplets, they came out like triplets.
That's right. This particular record I heard just wasn't clear or precise. That's why I said that wasn't Freddy.
